core_obligations: Reduce to a curve (proof lines 15386-15392): a smooth X is a finite disjoint union of smooth curves and points; the higher cohomology of any sheaf on the spectrum of k is trivial, so one may assume X is a smooth curve.

Case I, ell different from the characteristic (proof lines 15394-15408): the projective case is the cohomology-of-a-smooth-projective-curve lemma and the affine case the vanishing-of-mu lemma; the base change statement under extension of the algebraically closed ground field follows because the genus and the number of punctures do not change, and the surjectivity statement follows because H^2_etale(U, F) vanishes whenever U is a proper open subset, U being then affine.

Case II, ell equal to the characteristic (proof lines 15410-15414): vanishing is the characteristic-p vanishing lemma, and the finiteness and proper base change statements follow from the characteristic-p finiteness lemma.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a smooth curve using the decomposition into curves and points and the triviality on a point.
In the prime-to-characteristic case use the projective and affine computations, the invariance of genus and punctures, and the affineness of a punctured curve.
In the characteristic case use the vanishing and finiteness lemmas for varieties in characteristic p.
difficulty_reason: The lemma verifies the vanishing, finiteness, base change and surjectivity statements for the constant coefficient sheaf Z/ellZ on a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field (statement lines 15376-15383). The proof (proof lines 15385-15414) reduces to a smooth curve, treats the prime-to-characteristic case through the projective and affine computations with the invariance of genus and punctures and the affineness of punctured curves, and the characteristic case through the vanishing and finiteness lemmas in characteristic p. H2: two case analyses with named inputs, written out.
